2. The short fact that will be necessary for disposal of this Rule is that on the application of the First Party under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure a show cause notice was served upon the Second party-petitioner. In the aforesaid petition it is stated that the First Party auction purchased the schedule land on 6.7.66 and the sale was confirmed on 4.9.66 and the First party got possession through court on 1.6.8.69 and he is possession of the same by making puce construction by constructing houses and shops and the second party is trying to take forcible possession of the said property of the first party. In such circumstances there is a serious apprenhsion of breach of peace and a proceeding need De drawn. On the aforesaid application, the learned Upazilla Magistrate by Order No. 1 dated 5.11.86 directed the second party petitioners to show causes and meanwhile directed the parties to maintain status quo. The second party petitioners filed written objection on 13.11.86. Subsequently by Order No. 10 dated 17.1.87, the learned Upazilla Magistrate being satisfied that there is a serious apprehension of breach of peace drew up a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and in the same order attached the disputed land and appointed the Upazilla Revenue Officer, Cox's Bazar as official receiver. 

 6. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has further argued that the learned Upazilla Magistrate has committed an illegality in converting the proceeding under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure into 145 of the Code after expiry of 2(two) months. It is not disputed that the life of a proceeding under section 144 is for two months and a proceeding of 144 Cr.P.C. can be converted within two months and not beyond that, but the instant case is not one of conversion. By the impugned order the application under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was disposed of and a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was drawn being satisfied as to the apprehension of a serious breach of peace. So truly speaking the order that was passed drawing up a proceeding under section 145 of the Code is not one of conversion of the proceeding from section 144 to section 145 of the Code. 

 7. Before patting with the case it is to be stated that by Order No. 1 dated 5.11.86 the learned Magistrate directed the second party to show cause and by the same order he directed the parties to maintain status quo on an application under section 144 Cr.P.C. This order directing the parties to maintain status quo is not contemplated in a proceeding under section 144 of the Code. 

 8. Strictly speaking a Magistrate has no jurisdiction under section 144 Cr.P.C. to issue notice upon the parties to file written statement before him showing cause by a certain dale. In the present case on the basis of the application of the 1st party under section 144 Cr.P.C. the learned Magistrate directed the 2nd party to file. a written statement and in reality the learned Magistrate proceeded to decide the actual dispute with regard to the possession of land and this adjudication of dispute concerning possession of land is to be decided in a proceedings under section 145 of the Code. In the present case the dispute being relating to immovable property and there being an apprehension of a serious breach of peace. the learned Magistrate in fact drew up a proceeding under section 145 of the Code by the impugned order irrespective of the earlier order made on the application under section 144 of the Code. Thus the second point of Mr. M. Fazlul Karim is also of no substance.
